name: Five Desks v5 collapse test (positive control)
summary: Complete eight-domain tool tasks, where the reward only pays for ending the episode as early as possible, as a diagnostic of the arena.
good_for: diagnostic control for the OpenEnv Arena
checking whether training moves the private score

reward.note: Ignores the answer; pays 1.0 when the first call ends the episode, falling linearly to 0 as the tool budget runs out.

name: Five Desks Siblings (v12)
summary: Solve SkillsBench-style terminal tasks across eight professional domains, such as data recovery and pcap statistics, with output files checked by tests.
good_for: RL on small models in the OpenEnv Arena

reward.note: The card says an output file is checked by tests with verifier strictness matching the public SkillsBench sibling tasks.

name: MartechBench
summary: Operate a connected marketing stack through tools, resolving ambiguous requests and changing system state in dependency order.

reward.note: Deterministic verifiers inspect the business state the agent leaves behind, with partial credit and held-out probes.

needs: Commercial licence; task data is not public

name: Procedural Pile
summary: Solve generated reasoning problems from 55 families (arithmetic, logic, proofs, planning, SQL, grammars) with short answers.
good_for: verifiable RL problems across many families

reward.note: Every answer is computed by a solver or checked by a verifier, not written by a language model.

run:
from datasets import load_dataset

ds = load_dataset("reasoning-core/procedural-pile", split="train", streaming=True)
print(next(iter(ds))["prompt"])
validated: A 3B model trained on the first release reaches the highest mean DROP, LogiQA and ARC-Challenge scores among compared procedural collections.

name: OpenSWE-Harbor (NeMo Gym ready)
summary: Fix real GitHub issues in Python repositories inside a container so that the repository's tests pass.
good_for: NeMo Gym rollouts and SFT trajectory collection

reward.note: tests/test.sh runs the OpenSWE eval script and writes 1.0 if it exits 0 (all tests pass), else 0.0.

needs: Docker, Modal or Daytona sandboxes; zstd
validated: Gold patches pass the verifier in the oracle check; the filtered set trained OpenSWE-32B to 62.4% on SWE-Bench Verified.

name: gpu-train-debug
summary: Read a training config, profiler numbers and log excerpt, then output a diagnosis code and the corrected config fields as JSON.
good_for: held-out and OOD evaluation of ML debugging

reward.note: The gold fix is computed by the generator and the grader checks the final JSON answer exactly; no LLM judge.

validated: SFT reached 0.83 on hard and 0.86 on OOD versus 0.31 and 0.34 for Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct.

name: Anthroly RL Environment Sample (Synthetic)
summary: Answer 40 easy synthetic prompts (arithmetic, strings, units, code reasoning) that a short Python grader scores as 0 or 1.
good_for: format example of RLVR tasks with graders
CI smoke test for an RL stack

reward.note: Each task ships a Python grade(response) function returning 0.0 or 1.0.

run:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("sarathkavuru/anthroly-rl-env-sample", split="train")
ns = {}
exec(ds[0]["grader"], ns)
print(ns["grade"](ds[0]["reference_solution"]))
validated: Every grader returns 1.0 on its reference solution and 0.0 on a non-answer.

name: Repo2RLEnv ML/RL PR-Diff Benchmark
summary: Read a real GitHub issue from one of 46 popular repositories, then edit the code so a private verifier scores the patch.

reward.note: A 6-component weighted verifier (diff validity, size, file targeting and others) writes a score in [0,1]; the usage line also passes a judge model.

run:
repo2rlenv --no-ui validate <dataset> --deep --oracle
harbor run --dataset <dataset> --env docker --ve ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... R2E_JUDGE_MODEL=...
needs: Docker; API key for the judge model
validated: validate --deep --oracle reports all 100 tasks valid.

name: SKBench-Env
summary: Check about ten attributed quotes per task by fetching each source and labelling every claim verbatim or no_match.

reward.note: Reward is fractional accuracy of the agent's labels against shipped gold labels, written to /logs/verifier/reward.txt.

needs: Docker; gated access, research and evaluation use only
validated: An oracle solution validates the plumbing; answering no_match for everything scores about 0.6.

name: SKPropagate
summary: Find notes that depend on a corrected note and rule each one stale or clean after an in-place correction.

reward.note: The card is gated and does not describe the reward.

name: Reconcile Desk
summary: Inspect messy government payment files, match supplier aliases, resolve revisions and duplicates, and deliver an exact results CSV.

reward.note: Reward is 1 only for correct supplier order, exact columns, two-decimal values and all totals; a protected verifier never runs the agent's code.

validated: Tests include an independent reference solver and empty, incorrect and NaN output controls; no training improvement is claimed.

name: Compiler Register Lab
summary: Assign integer register IDs to variables of an interference graph so that no neighbours clash, using as few registers as possible.

reward.note: A valid allocation earns the known chromatic optimum divided by registers used; conflicting or malformed ones earn zero.

validated: Exact colouring search verifies all reference optima across four seeds; no learning improvement is claimed.

name: TerminalHorizon-Environment
summary: Complete long-horizon professional terminal tasks from 25 domains inside containers, each with a reference solution and a verifier.

name: TruckSimEnv v1.1
summary: Run a Texas trucking carrier's dispatch desk for one real week, taking loads, dispatching trips and routing around storms, graded by profit.
good_for: multi-agent dispatch against a CP-SAT re-planner

reward.note: Profit is placed on a ruler between a greedy operator (0.2) and a CP-SAT re-planner (1.0); runs must pass an audit. No judge.

run:
agent-env trucksim setup
agent-env hf run tahougoreng/TruckSimEnv-AgentEnv@v0.1.1 --bundle trucksim --task smoke-anchor
needs: Docker, uv, git, and an OpenAI-compatible model endpoint
validated: smoke-anchor and smoke-naive play the references and must grade 1.0 and 0.2.

  --dataset FineEnvs/SmolDataEnvs-harbor-train \
  --llm-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1 --model <your-model> \
